item.title: Air Plan Approval; District of Columbia; Enhanced Vehicle Emission Inspection and Maintenance (I/M) Program Revision and Basic I/M Program Certification for Moderate Nonattainment Areas Under the 2015 Ozone NAAQS — Federal Register — Documents Matching 'Maine'
item.description: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve a State Implementation Plan (SIP) revision submitted by the District of Columbia (DC, or the District). This revision incorporates regulatory updates made to the District's Enhanced motor vehicle emissions inspection and maintenance (I/M) program since the EPA's last SIP approval. The SIP revision also serves to certify that the District's existing Enhanced I/M program meets Clean Air Act (CAA) requirements for a Basic I/M program for the District's portion of the Washington, DC-MD-VA nonattainment area (the Washington nonattainment area) for the 2015 Ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standard (NAAQS).

item.title: Prohibiting Illegal Discrimination in Registered Apprenticeship Programs — Federal Register — Documents Matching 'Maine'
item.description: The Department of Labor (DOL or the Department) is issuing this final rule to remove the onerous and legally questionable affirmative action requirements that were previously imposed by the Department on Registered Apprenticeship program sponsors. This final rule also streamlines and simplifies nondiscrimination obligations for all program sponsors, while clarifying that sponsors are accountable for compliance with Federal and State nondiscrimination protections. It also makes conforming, technical changes to the Department's regulation that addresses Labor Standards for the Registration of Apprenticeship Programs.

item.title: Mullin v. Friends of the Ruidosa Church — U.S. Supreme Court — Slip Opinions (current Term)
item.description:
_________________ _________________ 1 Cite as: 610 U. S. ____ (2026) Per Curiam SUPREME COURT OF THE UNITED STATES No. 26A560 MARKWAYNE MULLIN, SECRETARY OF HOMELAND SECURITY, ET AL. v. FRIENDS OF THE RUIDOSA CHURCH, ET AL. ON APPLICATION FOR STAY [November 9, 2026] PER CURIAM. Section 102 of the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immi- grant Responsibility Act of 1996 (IIRIRA) grants the Secre- tary of Homeland Security broad authority to construct bor- der barriers and roads “to deter illegal crossings in areas of high illegal entry into the United States.” §102(a), 110 Stat. 3009–554, as amended, note following 8 U. S. C. §1103. The same section expressly authorizes the Secretary “ ‘to waive all legal requirements’ ” as “ ‘necessary to ensure expedi- tious construction’ ” of those barriers and roads, §102(c)(1), 119 Stat. 306, and sharply limits judicial review of all claims arising from such waiver determinations. Specifi - cally, the statute provides that “‘[a] cause of action or claim may only be brought alleging a violation of the Constitution of the United States’ ” and courts “ ‘shall not have jurisdic- tion’” over nonconstitutional claims. §102(c)(2)(A). Earlier this year, the Secretary invoked Section 102’s waiver authority to initiate a border-construction project at the U. S.–Mexico border, in a region that U. S. Customs and Border Protection has designated the “Big Bend Sector.” The Secretary found that the Big Bend Sector “is an area of high illegal entry” requiring additional border barriers, and waived the application of a variety of environmental and conservation laws to facilitate expeditious construction.

item.title: Medicare and Medicaid Programs; CY 2027 Payment Policies Under the Physician Fee Schedule and Other Changes to Part B Payment and Coverage Policies; Medicare Shared Savings Program Requirements; and Medicare Prescription Drug Inflation Rebate Program — Federal Register — Documents Matching 'Maine'
item.description: This final rule addresses: changes to the physician fee schedule (PFS); other changes to Medicare Part B payment policies to ensure that payment systems are updated to reflect changes in medical practice, relative value of services, and changes in the statute; codification of establishment of new policies for: the Medicare Prescription Drug Inflation Rebate Program under the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022; limiting Medicare coverage of certain individuals; the Ambulatory Specialty Model; updates to drugs and biological products paid under Part B; Medicare Shared Savings Program requirements; updates to the Quality Payment Program; updates to policies for Rural Health Clinics and Federally Qualified Health Centers; update to the Ambulance Fee Schedule regulations; codification of the Inflation Reduction Act and Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 provisions; updates to Clinical Laboratory Fee Schedule regulations; updates to the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program.

item.title: Calendar Year 2027 Home Health Prospective Payment System (HH PPS) Rate Update; Requirements for the HH Quality Reporting Program and the Expanded HH Value-Based Purchasing Model; Medicare Provider Enrollment, Durable Medical Equipment (DME), and DME, Prosthetics, Orthotics, and Supplies (DMEPOS) Policies — Federal Register — Documents Matching 'Maine'
item.description: This final rule sets forth routine updates to the Medicare home health payment rates in accordance with existing statutory and regulatory requirements. In addition, this final rule discusses the behavior adjustments and finalizes a temporary behavior adjustment. It also finalizes the recalibrated case-mix weights and updated functional impairment levels; comorbidity subgroups; and low-utilization payment adjustment (LUPA) thresholds for CY 2027. Additionally, this final rule discusses and responds to comments on the provision of home health palliative care services and includes a summary of comments received on the request for information (RFI) on a home health specific wage index included in the proposed rule. This rule also finalizes changes to the Home Health Quality Reporting Program (HH QRP) and summarizes potential initiatives to improve alignment between the HH QRP and expanded Home Health Value- Based Purchasing (HHVBP) Model. Lastly, the rule clarifies the application of the DMEPOS face-to- face encounter requirements for the replacement of DMEPOS items; makes changes to the provider and supplier enrollment requirements; makes changes to implement a DME benefit expansion for infusion pumps and drugs; and discusses collection of information requirement changes regarding the DMEPOS Competitive Bidding Program (CBP) country of origin.

item.title: Policy Statement on Jurisdiction and Preemption Under the ICC Termination Act — Federal Register — Documents Matching 'Maine'
item.description: The Surface Transportation Board (STB or Board) is issuing this policy statement on the scope of its jurisdiction over transportation by rail carriers and on preemption of conflicting state and federal laws under the ICC Termination Act of 1995 (ICCTA). The policy statement provides an overview of the Board's jurisdiction and preemption through a review of existing legal precedent, discussing many commonly occurring questions. The Board intends the policy statement to serve as a useful tool for the public to review, in one place, concise explanations from the Board about its jurisdiction and application of preemption, which the Board anticipates will reduce confusion and facilitate the efficient resolution of disputes.

item.title: Notice: Nationwide Email Service Disruption — U.S. District Court, District of Maine — News & Announcements
item.description: Thursday, November 12, 2026 The Court is currently experiencing a nationwide Microsoft email service disruption that is preventing the sending and receiving of emails, including filings submitted to the Court’s intake inboxes. The Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts (AO) is aware of the issue and is working to resolve it. At this time, there is no estimated timeframe for restoration of service. Parties with time-sensitive filings should submit them in paper format until email services are restored. Once service is restored, parties who are uncertain whether a filing submitted by email was received are encouraged to contact the Clerk’s Office to confirm receipt. We appreciate your patience and understanding.
item.content:encoded:
Thursday, November 12, 2026

The Court is currently experiencing a nationwide Microsoft email service disruption that is preventing the sending and receiving of emails, including filings submitted to the Court’s intake inboxes.
The Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts (AO) is aware of the issue and is working to resolve it. At this time, there is no estimated timeframe for restoration of service.
Parties with time-sensitive filings should submit them in paper format until email services are restored.
Once service is restored, parties who are uncertain whether a filing submitted by email was received are encouraged to contact the Clerk’s Office to confirm receipt.
We appreciate your patience and understanding.

item.title: Rangeland Management — Federal Register — Documents Matching 'Maine'
item.description: The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA or Department) proposes to amend the regulations governing grazing and livestock use on the National Forest System to modernize grazing administration, improve clarity, codify existing policy, and expand opportunities for stewardship and access. The proposed amendments would update permit issuance, eligibility, and qualification provisions; establish a framework for adaptive response to drought, wildfire, and similar disturbance events; and expand authorities for stewardship-oriented livestock use, including adding the ability to implement stewardship projects (such as outcome-based grazing or targeted grazing) under a temporary grazing permit or livestock use permit. The proposed rule would revise grazing fee provisions to ensure consistent fee-setting across the national forests in the 16 contiguous Western States and the national grasslands, and establish a surcharge for authorized leasing of livestock by permittees. It would consolidate and renumber existing sections in subpart A for clarity and make conforming, technical, and administrative updates throughout part 222. The Department invites public comment on all aspects of the proposed rule.

item.title: HIPAA Privacy Rule: Changes To Support Coordinated Care and Individual Engagement and Reduce Regulatory Burdens — Federal Register — Documents Matching 'Maine'
item.description: The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS or "Department") is issuing this final rule to modify the Standards for Privacy of Individually Identifiable Health Information ("Privacy Rule") under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) and the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health (HITECH) Act. These modifications address standards that may impede the nationwide transition to value-based health care by limiting or discouraging individual access or care coordination and case management or posing other unnecessary burdens. The modifications in this final rule promote the essential sharing of individuals' protected health information (PHI) for care coordination and individual engagement while continuing to protect its privacy and security.

These modifications address standards that may impede the nationwide transition to value-based health care by limiting or discouraging individual access or care coordination and case management or posing other unnecessary burdens. The modifications in this final rule promote the essential sharing of individuals' protected health information (PHI) for care coordination and individual engagement while continuing to protect its privacy and security.

item.title: Federal Financial Participation in State Assistance Expenditures; Federal Matching Shares for Medicaid, the Children's Health Insurance Program, and Aid to Needy Aged, Blind, or Disabled Persons for October 1, 2027, Through September 30, 2028 — Federal Register — Documents Matching 'Maine'
item.description: The Federal Medical Assistance Percentages (FMAP) and Enhanced Federal Medical Assistance Percentages (eFMAP) for fiscal year 2028 have been calculated pursuant to the Social Security Act (the Act). These percentages will be effective from October 1, 2027, through September 30, 2028. This notice announces the calculated FMAP rates, in accordance with the Act, that the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) will use in determining the amount of Federal matching for State medical assistance (Medicaid), Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) Contingency Funds, Child Support collections, Child Care Mandatory and Matching Funds of the Child Care and Development Fund, Title IV-E Foster Care Maintenance payments, Adoption Assistance payments and Kinship Guardianship Assistance payments, and the eFMAP rates for the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) expenditures. Table 1 gives figures for each of the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands. This notice reminds states of adjustments available for states meeting requirements for disproportionate employer pension or insurance fund contributions and adjustments for disaster recovery. At this time, no state qualifies for such adjustments, and territories are not eligible.
item.content:encoded: The Federal Medical Assistance Percentages (FMAP) and Enhanced Federal Medical Assistance Percentages (eFMAP) for fiscal year 2028 have been calculated pursuant to the Social Security Act (the Act). These percentages will be effective from October 1, 2027, through September 30, 2028. This notice announces the calculated FMAP rates, in accordance with the Act, that the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) will use in determining the amount of Federal matching for State medical assistance (Medicaid), Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) Contingency Funds, Child Support collections, Child Care Mandatory and Matching Funds of the Child Care and Development Fund, Title IV-E Foster Care Maintenance payments, Adoption Assistance payments and Kinship Guardianship Assistance payments, and the eFMAP rates for the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) expenditures. Table 1 gives figures for each of the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands. This notice reminds states of adjustments available for states meeting requirements for disproportionate employer pension or insurance fund contributions and adjustments for disaster recovery. At this time, no state qualifies for such adjustments, and territories are not eligible.
